contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

As the construction foreman, pick a start time for each activity which has a fixed duration, uses limited crews and machines while it runs, and may require that some activities finish before others begin, and make sure overlapping activities never demand more crews or machines than are available while aiming to complete the whole build as early as possible.

As the head chef, set a start time for every recipe step that has a set cooking time, consumes limited kitchen equipment or staff during its execution, and depends on certain previous steps finishing before it can start, ensuring that at no moment do simultaneous steps exceed the available ovens or cooks and schedule to get service finished as soon as you can.

As the film director, assign starting moments for each shooting scene that lasts a fixed amount of time, requires particular camera teams and props while it is filmed, and cannot begin until specified prior scenes are wrapped, making sure total demand for each crew and prop does not exceed what is on hand and aiming to finish the shoot as early as possible.

As the software release manager, decide a start time for each development task with fixed effort duration that consumes constrained developer hours and testing servers during its run and that may depend on earlier tasks being completed, and ensure concurrent tasks never use more developer time or server capacity than available while minimizing the date when the full release is ready.

As the event planner, choose start times for all setup and program items that each take a fixed amount of time, draw on limited volunteers and equipment while active, and require certain earlier items to be completed before they start, ensuring that at any time volunteer and equipment needs do not exceed supply and aiming to have the whole event ready as early as possible.

As the manufacturing supervisor, schedule start times for every production operation that has a fixed run time, consumes limited machines and operators while running, and follows prescribed predecessor operations, making certain that simultaneous operations do not demand more machines or operators than available and striving to minimize the time when the final product is completed.

As the head nurse, assign start times for each patient procedure which lasts a fixed time, occupies limited operating rooms and staff while underway, and must wait for certain prior procedures to finish, ensuring overlapping procedures never exceed room or staff availability and working to bring the overall ward schedule to completion as early as possible.

As the shipyard foreman, set starting times for all repair jobs that each have a fixed duration, require limited cranes and crews while in progress, and depend on other jobs being completed first, while ensuring that at any point the sum of crane and crew needs does not surpass what is available and aiming to finish the entire refit as soon as possible.

As the gardening coordinator, pick start times for every landscaping task that has a fixed length, uses limited tractors and crew while occurring, and cannot start until some preparatory tasks are done, making sure concurrent tasks never demand more equipment or workers than are available and scheduling to complete the garden project at the earliest possible moment.

As the furniture shop owner, choose start times for each assembly step which lasts a fixed period, consumes limited tools and bench space while active, and must follow certain earlier steps, ensuring that simultaneous steps do not exceed the available tools and benches and aiming to finish the whole batch as early as possible.

As the school principal, schedule start times for each classroom setup and session that have fixed durations, require limited rooms and teachers while running, and depend on some other sessions finishing first, making sure room and teacher usage never exceed the school resources at any time and striving to end the schedule as soon as possible.

As the photographer, assign starting times for every shoot segment that lasts a fixed time, uses limited lighting rigs and crew while underway, and depends on earlier segments being completed, ensuring overlapping segments do not exceed available rigs or personnel and planning to conclude the shoot at the earliest feasible time.

As the music producer, decide start times for all recording sessions which each have a fixed duration, occupy constrained studio space and engineers while recording, and cannot begin until certain prior tracks are done, while ensuring that simultaneous sessions never demand more studio time or engineers than available and aiming to finish the album as early as possible.

As the lab manager, set start times for every experiment run that has a fixed runtime, consumes limited instruments and technician hours while active, and follows required prior experiments, ensuring that at any moment instrument and technician demand does not exceed supply and scheduling to get all experiments completed as soon as possible.

As the warehouse manager, pick starting times for each picking and packing job that each last a fixed period, use limited forklifts and staff while in progress, and must wait for certain preceding jobs to finish, making sure that combined forklift and staff needs at any time do not exceed availability and aiming to ship the whole batch at the earliest possible time.

As the landscape architect, choose start times for every hardscape and planting phase that have fixed durations, draw on limited crews and equipment while ongoing, and require that specific earlier phases finish first, ensuring concurrent phases never demand more crew or kit than are available and aiming to complete the project as early as possible.

As the festival organizer, schedule start times for each vendor stall setup and performance block that lasts a fixed interval, consumes limited setup teams and power supplies while active, and depends on other setups being finished before they begin, ensuring that at no time do overlaps exceed team or power capacity and working to have the entire festival ready as early as possible.

As the home renovator, assign start times for each renovation task which has a fixed span, uses limited tradespeople and tools while underway, and must follow certain preparatory jobs, ensuring overlapping tasks do not require more trades or tools than available and striving to finish the renovation project as soon as possible.

As the relief coordinator, decide start times for all distribution activities that have fixed durations, use limited trucks and volunteers while they run, and depend on certain prior activities finishing before they start, while ensuring overlapping activities never demand more vehicles or volunteers than available and aiming to complete the whole relief operation as early as possible.

As the caterer preparing for a large reception, assign start times to every cooking and plating step with set durations, knowing each step uses limited kitchen equipment and staff and that certain steps depend on the completion of earlier steps, and arrange the sequence to minimize the moment when the last dish is ready while never exceeding available equipment or staff.

As the moving company coordinator, choose start times for every loading and transport job with fixed durations, where jobs use limited trucks and crews while underway and some jobs depend on earlier jobs finishing, and lay out the schedule to complete the move as early as possible without exceeding vehicle or crew capacities.

As the publishing editor managing layout and proofing, set start times for every editorial task that takes a fixed amount of time, recognizing tasks draw on limited proofreaders and layout stations while active and certain tasks must follow others, and schedule them to minimize the time when the final manuscript is ready while not exceeding resource limits.

As the wardrobe stylist preparing for a runway show, plan start times for every fitting and alteration task with set durations, noting each task uses scarce sewing machines and stylists while in progress and that some fittings wait on previous tweaks, and arrange starts so the entire collection is ready as soon as possible without going over equipment or stylist capacity.

As the TV broadcast scheduler, assign start times to every segment preparation job that has a fixed length, where jobs consume limited studios and crews while running and some segments depend on the completion of prior preparations, and sequence them to minimize when the broadcast lineup is fully ready while ensuring resources are never overbooked.

As the appliance repair shop manager, schedule start times for every diagnostic and repair job that runs for a fixed period, with each job consuming limited benches and technicians while in progress and some repairs awaiting parts from earlier diagnostics, and organize the schedule to minimize when the last appliance is fixed while respecting bench and technician limits.

As aircraft maintenance chief, plan start times for each maintenance job that takes a fixed duration and occupies hangar bays and technicians while it runs, with some jobs needing inspections done first, with the objective to return the fleet to service as early as possible while never exceeding hangar or staff limits.

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: task_id

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: successors

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands

task_item_fields.name: successors

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: demands

task_item_fields.name: successors

global_fields.name: nr_tasks

global_fields.name: nr_resources

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: task_id

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Vector of integers, one per resource type, indicating how many units of each resource the job requires while it runs (e.g., number of trucks and number of crews consumed during this job). These demands must not cause the per-time resource usage to exceed resource_capacities.

task_item_fields.name: successors
task_item_fields.scenario_description: List of job_ids that cannot start until this job has finished. Represents precedence relations (e.g., a transport cannot start until the corresponding loading job finishes). The solver must ensure these successors' start times are at or after this job's end time.

global_fields.name: nr_tasks

global_fields.name: nr_resources
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different limited resource types available on the editorial floor (each resource type is a staff role or piece of equipment, for example proofreader, senior proofreader, layout station). This is the length of each demand vector and of the capacities vector.

global_fields.name: capacities
global_fields.scenario_description: A list giving the available quantity of each resource type (in the same order as the implicit resource types). For example [3,2] could mean 3 proofreaders and 2 layout stations. These capacities cannot be exceeded at any time.

task_item_fields.name: task_id
task_item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the editorial task (e.g., an index or short label). This is used to reference the task in precedence lists and in the final schedule.

task_item_fields.name: duration
task_item_fields.scenario_description: The fixed processing time the task requires, expressed in a consistent time unit across all tasks (hours or days). Once started, the task occupies its demanded resources for this entire duration.

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: A vector of nonnegative integers, length equal to resource_types_count, specifying how many units of each resource type the task needs while it runs (e.g., [1,0] uses one proofreader and no layout station). The order of entries matches resource_capacities.

task_item_fields.name: successors

global_fields.name: nr_tasks

global_fields.name: nr_resources

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: task_id

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands

task_item_fields.name: successors
task_item_fields.scenario_description: List of fitting_ids that must start only after this fitting finishes. Represents the precedence relations (tweaks that wait on earlier adjustments).

global_fields.name: nr_tasks

global_fields.name: nr_resources

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: task_id
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the segment preparation job (the specific 'dish'). Used to reference this job in dependencies and the schedule.

task_item_fields.name: duration
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Fixed time length required to prepare this segment (how long the dish must cook). The job occupies its demanded resources for this entire interval after its chosen start time.

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: A vector of integers (same order and length as resource_capacities) giving how many units of each resource this segment needs while running, e.g. [studios_needed, crews_needed]. These demands must be met simultaneously for the whole prep_time.

task_item_fields.name: successors
task_item_fields.scenario_description: List of segment_ids that cannot start until this segment has finished. Interpreted as finish-to-start precedence constraints: every listed successor must have a start time >= this segment's finish time.

global_fields.name: nr_tasks

global_fields.name: nr_resources
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct limited resource types used by jobs (in this shop scenario typically 2: benches and technicians).

global_fields.name: capacities
global_fields.scenario_description: List of integers giving the available capacity for each resource type. The order of this list determines the indices used in each job's demand vector (for example [benches_available, technicians_available]).

task_item_fields.name: task_id
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the job (diagnostic or repair). Used to reference the job in precedence relations and the final schedule.

task_item_fields.name: duration
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Fixed time the job occupies required resources while running. Expressed in the same time units for all jobs (e.g., minutes or hours).

task_item_fields.name: demands

task_item_fields.name: successors

global_fields.name: nr_tasks

global_fields.name: nr_resources

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: task_id

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands

task_item_fields.name: successors

task_item_fields.scenario_description: List of block_ids that are required to start only after this block finishes. May be empty. These encode the rehearsal ordering constraints (precedences).

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: task_id
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific repair activity or road segment job; used to reference the task in dependencies and the schedule.

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Vector of resource usage while the repair runs, aligned with resource_capacities (e.g., [crews_required, machines_required]). These amounts are consumed for the whole task duration.

task_item_fields.name: successors

global_fields.name: capacities

task_item_fields.name: task_id

task_item_fields.name: duration
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Fixed running time of the task (expressed in minutes) from its start until it finishes; the task occupies its required resources for this whole duration.

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Vector of integers giving how many units of each resource type the task requires while running, listed in the same order as resource_capacities (e.g., [forklifts_required, floor_staff_required]).

task_item_fields.name: successors

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: successors

task_item_fields.name: demands

task_item_fields.name: successors

task_item_fields.name: successors
task_item_fields.scenario_description: List of task_ids that are constrained to start only after this task has finished. An empty list means no direct successors. These entries define the precedence constraints the schedule must respect.

global_fields.name: nr_tasks
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct ground service activities that must be scheduled for this aircraft (e.g., fueling, catering, cleaning). This is the number of task entries the schedule must assign start times to.

global_fields.name: nr_resources
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of different resource types available to the ground crew (each type is a separate limited resource, e.g., fuel truck units, catering vans, ramp agents). This defines the length of each resource vector.

global_fields.name: capacities
global_fields.scenario_description: A list (vector) giving the available amount/capacity of each resource type while scheduling (in the same order as resource types). At any time the sum of demands from running activities cannot exceed these capacities.

task_item_fields.name: task_id

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: A vector of the amounts of each resource type this activity requires while it is running (ordered to match resource_capacities). These demands are counted continuously from the activity start until start + activity_duration.

task_item_fields.name: successors

task_item_fields.name: task_id

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands

task_item_fields.name: successors

global_fields.name: nr_tasks

global_fields.name: nr_resources
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of distinct resource kinds used by activities (for example: studio time slots and editors). This indicates how many entries each task demand vector and the capacities vector will contain, and defines the resource dimensions the scheduler must respect.

global_fields.name: capacities
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of available capacity for each resource type (in the same order implied by resource_types). For example, the first entry might be the number of studio slots available at any time and the second the number of editors available concurrently. The scheduler may not assign simultaneous activities whose summed demands exceed these capacities.

task_item_fields.name: task_id
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the activity (a shoot or an edit). Used to reference the activity in precedence relations and in the output schedule; must match identifiers used in successors lists.

task_item_fields.name: duration

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Vector of resource usage while the activity runs, with one entry per resource type in the same order as resource_capacities (e.g., [studio_slots, editors]). Each entry is the amount of that resource consumed for the activity's whole duration. At any time the sum of demands of overlapping activities must not exceed the corresponding capacities.

task_item_fields.scenario_description: Fixed run time of the activity in project time units. The activity occupies its demanded resources for the interval [start, start + activity_duration).

task_item_fields.name: demands
task_item_fields.scenario_description: Vector of integers specifying how many units of each resource the activity requires while running. The order matches resource_capacities (e.g. [build_machines_needed, test_environments_needed]).

task_item_fields.name: successors
task_item_fields.scenario_description: List of activity_ids that must start only after this activity has finished (direct successors). All such precedence constraints must be satisfied in the schedule.
